territorial_scope.description: EU-wide framework applying across all Member States, with each Member State designating national cybersecurity certification authorities in its territory; no extraterritorial reach is stated.

evidence.quote: Each Member State shall designate one or more national cybersecurity certification authorities in its territory

summary.short: Regulation (EU) 2019/881 establishes ENISA as the EU Agency for Cybersecurity and creates an EU framework for voluntary cybersecurity certification of ICT products, services and processes, with basic, substantial and high assurance levels. It repeals Regulation (EU) No 526/2013 with effect from 27 June 2019.
summary.long: The Regulation sets out ENISA's objectives, tasks and organisation. ENISA advises the Union and Member States, supports capacity-building, incident response and operational cooperation (including the CSIRTs network secretariat), organises cybersecurity exercises, prepares situation reports, promotes awareness and cyber-hygiene, and analyses cybersecurity markets and standards. Its governance comprises a Management Board, an Executive Board, an Executive Director, an ENISA Advisory Group and a National Liaison Officers Network. Title III establishes the European cybersecurity certification framework. The Commission adopts certification schemes by implementing acts, based on candidate schemes prepared by ENISA. Schemes may specify assurance levels basic, substantial or high, and may allow conformity self-assessment only for basic. Certification is voluntary unless Union or Member State law provides otherwise. Manufacturers or providers of certified or self-assessed products must make supplementary cybersecurity information publicly available. Conformity assessment bodies are accredited by national accreditation bodies for a maximum of five years. Each Member State designates national cybersecurity certification authorities that supervise compliance, handle complaints and may withdraw certificates. Member States may not introduce new national schemes for products already covered by an EU scheme. Member States lay down penalties that must be effective, proportionate and dissuasive.

notes: The supplied text runs from the preamble to Art. 68 (Title IV); the Annex referred to in Art. 60(1) is not included in this part. Art. 22 names the 'Stakeholder Cybersecurity Certification Group', but Art. 22(4) and Art. 47(4) refer to the 'Stakeholder Certification Group'. Relation rows use an empty target_instrument_id where the target has no registry ID in the supplied material. Part 2 of 2 covers Article 69 (entry into force on the twentieth day after OJ publication; Articles 58, 60, 61, 63, 64 and 65 apply from 28 June 2021) and the Annex (requirements for conformity assessment bodies). Internal references to Articles of this Regulation (e.g., Article 61 in Annex point 10(b)) are not coded as relations. The only external instrument cited in an operative provision of this part is Regulation (EC) No 765/2008. Footnotes in this part are not numbered in the operative text; the cited instruments in the footnotes are not coded here. No internal inconsistency found in this part.
